**Allowed origins** are set in the `origin` callback passed to `cors({...})` in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It echoes the request origin back if any of these hold:
- It is exactly `http://localhost:4200`.
- It ends with `.pages.dev`, which covers any depth.
- It ends with `.workers.dev`, which covers any depth.

Anything else, including a request with no `Origin` header, gets `null`, so no CORS headers are sent. The same middleware also sets:
- `allowMethods`: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS.
- `allowHeaders`: Content-Type, Authorization.
- `maxAge`: 86400.

**Adding a custom domain:** edit the `if` condition at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. Add another `||` clause inside the `origin: (origin) => {...}` function, for example `origin === 'https://app.example.com'`. Use an exact match, because a suffix check like `endsWith('example.com')` would also match `evilexample.com`.

Don't put the domain in an array. Hono matches array entries as exact strings, and the file's comment at line 20 says the same. `worker/src/index.md:24-25` and `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 (CORS) cover this too.

After the change, update the CORS line in `worker/src/index.md:7` to match, as `docs/AUTHORING.md` requires. I didn't read `AUTHORING.md`, so I can't say what else it asks for.

I made no changes, as you asked.
